name: GA-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+15 partisan lean strongly favors Republicans
Incumbent Brian Jack holds a massive fundraising edge ($2.0M raised vs. $150K for Keller)
Prediction markets price the Republican at about 96%
First-term incumbent renominated with no expert raters flagging the race
model.rationale: The district's fifteen-point Republican lean, Jack's roughly thirteen-to-one fundraising advantage, and a 96% Republican price on prediction markets leave Keller without a realistic path; no polls or expert ratings point to competitive conditions.
model.watch: A major scandal involving the incumbent or a sharp national shift toward Democrats could narrow the margin, though the district's fundamentals make an upset very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Georgia's 3rd District is firmly Republican territory, with a partisan lean of roughly fifteen points toward the GOP. Brian Jack, a first-term incumbent who won the seat in 2024, is running for re-election and faces Democrat Maura Keller. Jack has built an overwhelming financial advantage, raising about $2.0 million to Keller's $150,000 and holding more than $1.1 million on hand entering the general election.

No public polls cover the race, and prediction markets give Republicans about a 96% chance of holding the seat. With Jack renominated without difficulty and no outside spending directed at the district, the structural ingredients for an upset are absent. The forecast expects Jack to win by a comfortable double-digit margin in November.
